notes: Stress variant: captions off (the label stack is the caption), 11 rows with no per-row t (default pacing: rowsT 0 so frame 1 has the start row landed, rowEvery 0.7, plus the kit's 1.2 s pause after the event row), wide 6-digit values with ≈ in narrow side-by-side panels, a long plan that wraps to three lines, an event with markup on a bad row, an event on the last row (goal), a mark on a cell, the summary as a coral TOTALS line (too wide for the panels) under the last row of the final table (7 of 12 lines fit at 44 px: the first row, the crash-tone event row, the last row and the totals stay, evenly spread plain rows fill the rest), a working beat, a two-line footer and a two-line verdict with a coral emphasis. Both invest $100,000 once at 35, nothing added. Market return 7% a year before fees; the fee is taken as a share of the balance each year, so the net growth factor is 1.07 × (1 − fee). Priya 0.05%: 1.069465 a year; Marcus 1%: 1.0593 a year. Balances at 35 + n (n = 0, 3, …, 30), rounded to the nearest $1,000 on screen: 38 $122,321 / $118,866; 41 $149,623 / $141,291; 44 $183,020 / $167,946; 47 $223,872 / $199,631; 50 $273,841 / $237,293; 53 $334,964 / $282,060 (gap $52,904, the first above $50,000; at 50 it is $36,548); 56 $409,730 / $335,273; 59 $501,185 / $398,525; 62 $613,052 / $473,710; 65 $749,890 / $563,079. Gap at 65: $186,811 (≈ $187,000; also $750,000 − $563,000 on the rounded figures). 'Fees took' = the no-fee balance ($100,000 × 1.07^30 = $761,226) minus each balance: Priya $11,336 (≈ $11,000), Marcus $198,147 (≈ $198,000).
